about: Lock 1 Distilling Company sits on Culvert Street in Phoenix, across the road from Lock 1 of the Oswego Canal, a waterway the distillery says bootleggers favored for running Canadian liquor south during Prohibition. Three Phoenix-born cousins, Brenden Backus, Stephen Dates and Kevin Dates, founded it in 2015, and it is the first distillery to open in Oswego County since Prohibition. Backus, the master distiller, also runs a welding and fabrication shop, so the family built most of the equipment themselves, still included.

Lock 1 is a New York farm distillery, which means most of what goes into the still is grown in the state, and the cousins work from grain to glass on site. This coconut whiskey starts from a wheat whiskey base, which is then flavored with toasted coconut and bottled at 80 proof. The distillery says the idea began as a campfire experiment and won over doubters, from serious whiskey drinkers to people new to whiskey.

Lock 1 describes a smooth, sweet whiskey with lingering toasted coconut, a light touch of oak and a soft, nutty finish. It is meant to be sipped neat or used in place of a plain whiskey or rum in cocktails, where the coconut works in tiki-style drinks and in a coconut take on the Old Fashioned.
